The title of this song itself shallows love as a feeling. There is more to actual love, than just sexuality. And seeing a line like "My body isn't ready" for the first time, I thought to myself: "So now they advertise potence medicines in form of music videos"? Then it came to my mind that this song is about a teenager, who's gone through some massive body shaming and now is reluctant about dates due to that. If so, here's a piece of advice for all you teenagers, who empathise with the guy from this song. Love isn't about being pretty, or ugly, it's about caring, understanding and being responsible for each other. And as for the way your body looks, most imperfections are fixable and should never impair your perception in the loved one's eyes. If it does, just turn your back on them and go - it's not a real love, if he/she can only love you for something you have, not despite of something you lack, like an attractive bodily appearance. And before one says that I am here to criticise only (what is actually not true anyway), kudos to you for providing like an alternate ending to the "Obsession" movie. It is totally like shuttled out of a bag labeled "Things nobody asked for, but which everyone needed".

Amidst the race to meet standards and the pressure of excessive expectations, it is crucial not to lose yourself and to remain true to who you are until the very end. Sometimes we meet people who see right through us. I mean people who say: "I see your wounds and scars, and I still want to stay with you. I feel your pain and accept it as my own, and I still want to be by your side." Often, people push someone like that away or run off. But one day, you will let someone love you and let someone heal you. That journey is never easy. It is a constant cycle of ups and downs, doubt and mistrust. Yet, deep down, each of us holds a certain faith. A faith that is hard to shatter with the opinions of others, judgment, or societal criticism. It is a true, primal belief that we are accepted for who we really are, and that even with our ugly scars, we are still needed by someone. It is always a personal choice whether to run or to stay. But I hope that there will be more kindness and compassion in this world, and that love will once again work its magic.
